content: Penicillin G Procaine is an antibiotic approved by the FDA for treating severe infections caused by penicillin-G-susceptible microorganisms, including streptococci, pneumococci, syphilis, and fusospirochetosis. It is used in both adults and pediatric patients. Common adverse reactions include allergic responses and pseudomembranous colitis. For adults, Penicillin G Procaine is indicated for moderately severe infections caused by susceptible microorganisms. Therapy should be guided by bacteriological studies and clinical response. When high, sustained serum levels are required, aqueous penicillin G (IM or IV) is preferred. Infections such as upper respiratory tract infections, skin and soft tissue infections, scarlet fever, and erysipelas caused by Group A streptococci (without bacteremia) typically respond to intramuscular Penicillin G Procaine. However, aqueous penicillin is recommended for streptococcal infections with bacteremia. Pneumococcal respiratory infections, moderately severe skin infections caused by penicillin-G-susceptible staphylococci, and fusospirochetosis (Vincent's gingivitis and pharyngitis) are also treated with this drug. Necessary surgical or dental procedures should accompany therapy when indicated. Penicillin G Procaine is also used for syphilis (all stages), yaws, bejel, pinta, diphtheria (as an adjunct to antitoxin), anthrax (cutaneous and inhalational post-exposure), rat-bite fever, erysipeloid, and subacute bacterial endocarditis in highly sensitive infections. It is not recommended for beta-lactamase-producing organisms, including most strains of Neisseria gonorrhea. The drug is administered via deep intramuscular injection, avoiding injection near arteries or nerves to prevent permanent neurological damage. Injection sites should be varied for repeated doses. Dosage recommendations include 600,000 to 1,000,000 units daily for moderately severe pneumococcal pneumonia, streptococcal infections, and staphylococcal infections. Pediatric patients under 60 pounds may receive 300,000 units daily for pneumonia and streptococcal or staphylococcal infections. For syphilis, primary, secondary, and latent stages require 600,000 units daily for 8 days, while late syphilis may require 10-15 days of treatment. Congenital syphilis in children under 70 pounds is treated with 50,000 units/kg/day for 10 days. For inhalational anthrax post-exposure, adults receive 1,200,000 units every 12 hours, and children receive 25,000 units/kg every 12 hours (maximum 1,200,000 units). Therapy for inhalational anthrax must continue for 60 days. Penicillin G Procaine is contraindicated in patients with a history of hypersensitivity to penicillin. Serious hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, have been reported, especially in individuals with a history of penicillin or multiple allergen sensitivities. If an allergic reaction occurs, the drug should be discontinued, and appropriate therapy, including epinephrine, oxygen, IV steroids, and airway management, should be initiated. Pseudomembranous colitis has been reported with nearly all antibacterial agents, including Penicillin G. Symptoms may occur during or after antibiotic treatment. Mild cases usually resolve with drug discontinuation, while moderate to severe cases may require fluid and electrolyte management, protein supplementation, and treatment with an antibacterial effective against Clostridium difficile. Penicillin G Procaine is excreted in human milk, so caution is advised when administered to nursing mothers. In neonates and individuals with impaired renal function, drug elimination may be delayed. Elderly patients may require cautious dose selection due to the higher likelihood of decreased renal, hepatic, or cardiac function. Penicillin G Procaine exerts bactericidal action by inhibiting cell-wall biosynthesis in penicillin-susceptible microorganisms during active multiplication. It is not effective against penicillinase-producing bacteria. The drug is distributed throughout body tissues, with the highest levels in the kidneys and lesser amounts in the liver, skin, and intestines. It is excreted rapidly by tubular excretion in individuals with normal kidney function. Penicillin G Procaine is supplied as a stable aqueous suspension for intramuscular injection, eliminating the need for diluents. It is available in pre-filled syringes containing 600,000 or 1,200,000 units. The product should be stored in a refrigerator at 2° to 8°C (36° to 46°F) and protected from freezing.
